argument_summary: The record does not support an unqualified statement that rollout controls cured the weakness. It does support a narrower certification basis: aggregate launch readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents were observed, and public governance guidance supports disclosure plus deployment monitoring. Under the stated policy, certification is supportable only as a caveated path contingent on explicit pre-launch model-card disclosure of the clinical-trial intake limitation for the named launch use case, because the affected segment remains exposed and the draft risk acceptance is neither approved nor scoped to that exposure.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is offered as a basis to override policy. The relevant point is limited: if the packet is framed as caveated compliance rather than escalation-worthy noncompliance, remaining uncertainty can be handled by requiring the disclosure condition in the certification record instead of treating the whole launch basis as unsupported.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not permit treating the 8% rollout, random site gating, rollback switch, or dashboard as a substitute for disclosure while the affected clinical-trial intake segment remains exposed. The admissible evidence supports a policy-consistent packet only if the certification claim is narrowed to: readiness evidence supports launch, and disclosure is the required condition that makes certification compliant on this record. The audit concern is correct as to any unqualified certification claim, but overbroad if it treats the entire certification position as unsupported rather than condition-dependent.
concessions: No admissible evidence currently shows the actual pre-launch model card or equivalent approved artifact containing the required disclosure.
The unsigned risk-acceptance draft does not satisfy the policy substitute condition and cannot be cited as approved coverage for the exposed segment.
Rollout controls alone do not eliminate disclosure duties for the clinical-trial intake segment.
